newsitem.title: INDIA: New Holland eyes 15 pct of India tractor mkt.
newsitem.headline: New Holland eyes 15 pct of India tractor mkt.

text.p: Agricultural equipment maker New Holland hopes to capture 15 percent of the Indian tractor market over the next seven years, company officials said on Wednesday.
"We see some 15 percent share over a period of seven years," New Holland president and chief executive officer Umberto Quadrino told a news conference.
New Holland is controlled by Dutch-registered New Holland NV, a subsidiary of Fiat Spa, and began trading on Wall Street in November last year after a public share offering.

The firm, which obtained approval from the Indian government in 1996 to set up a wholly owned subsidiary, New Holland Tractors (India) Pvt Ltd, said it planned to make an initial investment of $50 million in a tractor manufacturing plant.
It said the plant in Greater Noida, in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh, would make Ford-branded tractors in the 35- to 75-horsepower range.
"The market is bullish at this very moment. There is a good potential in this market," Quadrino later told Reuters.
He said liberalisation of the Indian economy had spurred New Holland into setting up a subsidiary.
India began deregulating its economy in 1991, opening up industry and trade to private and foreign investors after decades of socialist controls.
"This was one of reasons we decided to look at India with a different point of view," Quadrino said.
The Uttar Pradesh government has offered New Holland a 12-year sales tax waiver, a government official said.

The new plant's first phase would be capable of building 18,000 tractors per annum, a company statement said. New Holland planned to expand its annual capacity to up to 35,000 units over the next seven years, the firm's officials said.
The company expects the first tractor to roll out by January 1998. Initially, the tractors will be manufactured from completely knocked down kits (CKDs).
"Within three years, we will have three models," said Quadrino, without elaborating.
T.L. Palani Kumar, managing director of New Holland Tractors (India) Pvt Ltd, said the tractor market was growing at an average rate of seven percent compounded annually.
